Why would an external user care that a button was pressed?  This doesn't seem log-worthy.

The button event serves as a reminder that it was triggered manually by the user, 
not due to an unexpected reset, DC, or AC cycle. It is mainly used for debugging purposes

I'm not against this, our field support staff have been hinting to us that they want something like this as well.

However, since a press is always followed by a release, are events for both necessary?  What if we just had an event for button released with the press time in it, which is definitely known to the button code.  (assuming you're using phosphor-buttons)
Yes, this is a good point. If there are no other concerns, we can remove the pressed/released logs and only record ButtonStateChanged.
Done

What I was suggesting was to not generate 2 events for every button press and just do one on the release, including the button press time if that was useful.

Though I suppose even if both types of events are defined that doesn't mean they have to be used by the code generating the event.
Could you be more specific about the event format? Should we define the pass/release events and their timeline in a log format?

Right here https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-buttons/blob/master/src/power_button.cpp#L86  is where the code emits a signal saying a button was released, with the press time in the payload.  I was thinking the event could mirror that.  Just a single event with the press time in it.
Is this interface available for use in places other than phosphor-buttons? For example, the phosphor-gpio-monitor cannot obtain press time.

> Is this interface available for use in places other than phosphor-buttons? For example, the phosphor-gpio-monitor cannot obtain press time.

I don't know.

Phosphor-buttons can obtain the press time in the release function, but the time is not recorded in the log. Would it be possible to determine the press duration simply by checking the timestamp? Alternatively, we could set the resolved field to true, and then compare the timestamp with the updated_timestamp to determine the press time.

How about a proposal, call the event ButtonPressed or ButtonEngaged (ButtonStateChanged indicates that there might be state information in the arguments but we get none of that), arguments could be (1) ButtonName/ObjectPath (2) EngageDuration probably in milli-seconds or seconds.
Since phosphor-buttons have the available information to fill in the duration, this would work as is in that project. If you are monitoring GPIOs in phosphor-gpio-monitor, then you could either (a) throw an arbitrary time in the event or (b) maintain the assertion timestamp state elsewhere and use that in the de-assertion handler to populate the duration from the stored state and current timestamp.
Done
Don't we have an enum for this?  Rather than a free-form string?
Done
ButtonState was listed as primary but not included in the message.
Done
nit: how about a real button name here so we know what to exepct
